title: Choose the chat screen's structure
question: Fresh hand, same Loom palette. Lock one, steer, or re-roll.

options.label: Icon rail + conversation drawer
options.thesis: A 64px indigo rail holds the mark and actions; conversations live in a drawer grouped by day, so the transcript gets a wide 760px measure when the drawer is closed.
options.viewport: Rail left, drawer open beside it (closable), transcript centered at 760px, composer docked bottom.
options.risk: Switching conversations costs a click to open the drawer.

options.label: Turn ledger
options.thesis: The transcript reads like a ledger: a left gutter numbers every turn and shows its token count and version, so the machinery is visible line by line.
options.viewport: Indigo sidebar left; transcript rows with an 88px gutter (turn number, role, tokens, version) and 720px content; composer docked under the content column.
options.risk: Denser and less conversational than chat users expect; no bubbles to tell speakers apart at a glance.

options.label: Versions as tabs
options.thesis: Where you edited a prompt, its versions sit as tabs directly above that turn, making the message tree's branch points obvious and one click to switch.
materials: inline version tabs with madder underline
options.viewport: Indigo sidebar left; centered 720px column; a tab strip above any turn with siblings; composer docked bottom.
options.risk: Tabs repeat wherever branching happened; long conversations with many edits get noisy.
